papers.title: Enhancing cortical electrophysiological signatures of sleep overrides ER stress responses in sleep-deprived mice
papers.summary: In sleep-deprived mice, delivering flickering light stimulation (FLS) during sleep deprivation prevented the upregulation of activity-dependent and unfolded protein response (UPR)/ER-stress genes while further increasing NREM slow-wave activity, and induced brief neuronal OFF periods resembling a sleep-like cortical state. The authors conclude that physiological manipulation of cortical activity can dissociate ER-stress molecular signatures from electrophysiological markers of sleep pressure.

papers.title: Firing Without Wiring: How REM-like Sleep Reactivation Rebalances Excitation and Inhibition to Orthogonalize Memories
papers.summary: Using recurrent neural networks trained with Equilibrium Propagation, the study shows that REM-like sleep reduces memory interference by decorrelating task-specific neuronal populations through a mechanism termed reactivation-targeted pruning, where plasticity is confined to the most recently activated population and depressive excitatory input from older-memory populations. This mechanism held under Dale's law and required only excitatory synaptic depression, without inhibitory plasticity.

papers.title: iFLiP: accessible and low-cost lifetime fiber photometry for robust longitudinal and quantitative measurements of neural dynamics
papers.summary: Introduces iFLiP, a low-cost, off-the-shelf fluorescence lifetime fiber photometry system with turn-key software that monitors lifetime changes at up to 5000 Hz over days. Demonstrated utility by tracking PKA dynamics in vitro and in vivo, revealing striatal subregion- and cell-type-specific PKA dynamics during locomotion and previously unappreciated basal forebrain PKA activity linked to sleep/wakefulness.

papers.title: NED-Net: an annotation-training loop for rodent EEG event detection
papers.summary: The authors introduce NED-Net, open-source software for training and maintaining rodent EEG seizure detectors through an annotation-training loop that retrains on reviewed candidate events as annotations accumulate. A detector trained on one mouse cohort reached 93.6% precision, but failed to generalize (median per-animal recall 10%), and retraining with second-cohort annotations raised convulsive recall from 15% to 64%, detecting at least one reference seizure in every animal.

papers.title: BrainCodes: A Lightweight EEG Foundation Model over Discrete Neural Codes
papers.summary: Introduces BrainCodes, a lightweight EEG foundation model combining a quantization-based neural tokenizer with a spatiotemporal encoder, pretrained self-supervised on over 800 hours from more than 1,000 participants. It matches or surpasses state-of-the-art performance on sleep staging, attention assessment, and cognitive load estimation while using up to 97% fewer trainable parameters and transferring to low-resource wearable devices.

papers.title: From labels to latents: revealing state-dependent hippocampal computations and non-spatial replay with Jump Latent Variable Model
papers.summary: Proposes the Jump Latent Variable Model, an unsupervised EM-based latent variable model that infers population-activity latents and whether their dynamics are continuous or fragmented, without external labels. Applied to rodent hippocampus, it identifies a cholinergic-modulated continuity-fragmentation axis across sleep-wake states, reveals position-independent population patterns missed by supervised spatial decoding, and uncovers prevalent non-spatial pre-play and post-task locomotor replay.

papers.title: Sleep reactivation shapes memories of event and its temporal structure
papers.summary: In a preregistered study with 35 participants, closed-loop targeted memory reactivation (TMR) during slow-wave sleep enhanced recognition speed and confidence for cued event memories but impaired temporal-order memory immediately after sleep and attenuated its forgetting one week later. Stronger cue-elicited theta activity predicted better recognition of neutral content and poorer temporal-order memory.

papers.title: Daytime Napping and Associative-Memory Retrieval Speed: An Exploratory Behavioral and EEG Study
papers.summary: In a within-participant study with 15 healthy students, a 60-min daytime nap was associated with 6.7% faster delayed associative recognition compared to wakefulness, with the effect concentrated among slower responses. EEG showed aperiodic spectral slowing and stronger sigma activity after napping, but no EEG measure explained the response-time effect.

papers.title: Additive Effects of Time Awake and Number of Flights on Fatigue in Short-Haul Pilots: Implications for Duty Time Regulation.
papers.summary: Analyzed fatigue, subjective workload, and flight-associated hassles at the end of 553 short-haul flights from 37 airline pilots using linear mixed-models. Fatigue increased with time awake and number of flights and was higher when monitoring than flying, with the critical fatigue threshold exceeded 2.4 h earlier for four flights versus one, supporting a duty-time penalty for additional flights.

papers.title: Aperiodic neural activity predicts cortical excitability in TMS-EEG
papers.summary: Delivered single-pulse TMS to left M1 (n=29) and left DLPFC (n=11) in healthy adults during EEG and related pre-stimulus aperiodic and periodic activity to early local TMS-evoked potentials. The aperiodic exponent showed a strong negative relationship with EL-TEP amplitude in both regions, whereas alpha and beta power relationships were inconsistent, indicating aperiodic activity as a stronger marker of cortical excitability.

papers.title: Portable polysomnography-derived multi-domain EEG markers of anesthetic state transitions during propofol anesthesia for gastrointestinal endoscopy.
papers.summary: In 31 adults undergoing propofol anesthesia for gastrointestinal endoscopy, portable polysomnography-derived six-channel EEG showed stage-related changes in relative spectral power (delta decreased, theta/alpha/sigma/beta and SEF95 increased), spindle-like event density (highest during recovery), and functional connectivity (most widespread with amplitude envelope correlation). These findings identify candidate EEG markers for anesthetic state transitions.

papers.title: Inferring structural complexity from dynamical measures
papers.summary: Used Wilson-Cowan mean-field simulations across systematically rewired networks to map observational (spontaneous-activity) and perturbational complexity measures onto structural integration-differentiation balance and small-worldness. Perturbational measures robustly peaked at intermediate rewiring and scaled with small-worldness, whereas observational measures behaved heterogeneously, and perturbational complexity was highest in a wake-like near-critical regime and declined with sleep-like dynamics.

papers.title: Sleep, inflammation, and pain in musculoskeletal rehabilitation: a structured integrative review of neurobiological mechanisms and non-pharmacological pain management strategies.
papers.summary: This structured integrative review of 57 studies synthesized neurobiological mechanisms linking sleep disturbance, inflammation, and persistent pain, finding sleep restriction associated with changes in IL-6, TNF-α, and CRP and impaired descending pain inhibition. It concluded that exercise, manual therapy, electrical stimulation, laser therapy, and sleep-focused behavioral interventions have mechanistic plausibility but limited confirmatory trial evidence.

papers.title: Automated Interpretation of EEG Reports Using a Large Language Model with Structured Confidence Outputs
papers.summary: Developed a grammar-constrained Mistral-7B pipeline to extract structured diagnostic labels and confidence levels from free-text EEG reports and compared it with a second expert annotator and classical NLP baselines. Mistral-7B reached 96% Core Agreement with the reference annotator for overall abnormality (vs 98% between annotators) and detected rare epileptiform abnormalities missed by baselines; the structured task also transferred to MedGemma after prompt adaptation.

papers.title: A brain-behavior generative model links individual brain dynamics to perceptual decisions
papers.summary: Introduced a brain-behavior generative model in which whole-brain dynamics simulated on each participant's structural connectome generate single-trial EEG and reaction times during a motion discrimination task (n=17). Joint fitting reproduced individual ERPs and RT distributions, predicted fast versus slow held-out trials, and in silico silencing revealed person-specific sensorimotor and parietal contributions to decision speed.

papers.title: Water under the bridge: Aquatic environments and crepuscular-cathemeral intermediates facilitate temporal niche transitions in artiodactyls
papers.summary: Tested the crepuscular-cathemeral bridge hypothesis and environmental niche effects on temporal activity evolution in Artiodactyla by comparing aquatic Whippomorpha with terrestrial Ruminantia, including the first infraorder-wide cetacean activity database. Results supported a crepuscular-cathemeral bridge, with crepuscularity and cathemerality playing distinct roles, and showed aquatic Whippomorpha relied less on this bridge and lacked associated ecomorphological constraints.

papers.title: Entrainment of the Arabidopsis circadian clock to skeleton photoperiods
papers.summary: Used promoter-luciferase reporters to monitor the Arabidopsis circadian clock during entrainment to skeleton photoperiods and subsequent free-running conditions. Individual oscillator components entrained to skeleton photoperiods, and long skeleton photoperiods produced a phase jump in which the dusk light pulse was interpreted as dawn, mirroring phase jumps reported in rodent and insect behavior.

papers.title: Relationship between objective sleep efficiency and psychological distress in middle-aged and older Japanese: Results by work in the Shika study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional Shika study of 360 community-dwelling Japanese adults aged 40-90, actigraphy-measured low sleep efficiency was associated with psychological distress (K6) only among working women (β = -0.060, p = 0.013), with no such evidence in working or non-working men or non-working women.

papers.title: Integrating task-state electroencephalography and motor function for intelligent assessment of recovery status from prolonged disorders of consciousness.
papers.summary: Using task-state EEG and clinical records from 78 patients with prolonged disorders of consciousness, an SVM/logistic regression framework integrating alpha-band power spectral density and coherence measures with motor function scores achieved leave-one-out macro F1 of about 76%, with SHAP used for interpretation. The authors propose this as a preliminary intelligent assessment paradigm for recovery status.

papers.title: EEG-defined differences in functional networks following beta-band transcranial alternating current stimulation in patients with disorders of consciousness: a pilot study.
papers.summary: Applied 30-min frontal 20 Hz tACS (1 mA) to 28 patients with disorders of consciousness and measured fNIRS-based functional connectivity and graph metrics before and after stimulation. Stimulation was associated with transient FC enhancement and increased clustering, global and local efficiency with decreased path length at post-stim1, effects that were pathology-dependent and normalized by post-stim2, with Coma Recovery Scale-Revised scores correlating with connectivity and efficiency measures.

papers.title: EEG microstate alterations in psychotic depression: prolonged microstate C duration and associations with psychotic symptoms.
papers.summary: Comparing resting-state EEG microstates in 68 patients with psychotic major depression versus 63 with non-psychotic depression, the study found prolonged microstate C duration (91.99 vs 85.56 ms) and altered transition probabilities (increased B→A, decreased B→C and C→A). Reduced B→C transition probability was most strongly associated with thought disturbance (ρ=-0.393) and hostility, suggesting dysregulated perceptual-to-salience network coupling as a candidate marker of psychotic features.

papers.title: Progress in research on the bidirectional relationship between circadian rhythm and depression: A bibliometric analysis.
papers.summary: Bibliometric analysis of 444 Web of Science publications (2015-2025) on circadian rhythms and depression using VOSviewer and CiteSpace, showing markedly increased output after 2018, US leadership, and key themes including expression, sleep, circadian rhythms, and melatonin. The authors identify diagnosis, biomarker identification, individualized treatment, prognosis, and health management as likely future research directions.

papers.title: NeuroCodec: EEG-Guided Latent-Domain Generative Model for High-Fidelity Target Speaker Extraction
papers.summary: NeuroCodec is introduced as the first EEG-guided target speaker extraction framework operating in a neural audio codec latent space, using graph convolutions for spatial EEG dependencies, attention fusion, and Mamba temporal modeling with a six-phase training curriculum. It outperformed baselines on Cocktail Party and KUL datasets, achieved a mean listening score of 82.24 versus 49.63 for M3ANet, and enabled 44.1 kHz reconstruction extending to 20 kHz.

papers.title: The association of particulate matter 2.5 exposure with frailty trajectories in middle-aged and older Chinese adults and the potential modification by lifestyle and socioeconomic status.
papers.journal: Journal of occupational and environmental medicine
papers.summary: Analyzing 10,659 CHARLS participants with group-based trajectory modeling, the study identified three frailty trajectories and found each 10 μg/m³ increase in PM2.5 raised odds of the 'increased to frailty' and 'continuously worsening' trajectories by 15.2% and 12.3%, respectively. Higher socioeconomic status attenuated PM2.5 effects (RERI = -0.067), while unhealthy sleep duration amplified them (RERI = 0.163).

papers.title: Association of insomnia with anxiety might be greater than that of depression among patients with gastrointestinal cancer: a network analysis.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional network analysis of 352 gastrointestinal cancer patients, psychological distress prevalence was 45.2%, and the strongest partial correlation was between difficulty initiating sleep and anxiety (0.15), with no direct conditional association between depression and any insomnia symptom.

papers.title: Unilateral nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy associated with obstructive sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome: a case report.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 59-year-old Han Chinese man with unilateral nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy associated with obstructive sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome, who showed moderate improvement after oral methylprednisolone, neuroprotective and circulation-improving therapy, and noninvasive ventilation.

papers.title: The association between honey consumption amount and physical activity, sleep quality, and Nottingham health profile in young adults.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional comparative study of 468 university students in eastern Türkiye classified participants by daily honey intake (none to 40 g/day) and examined associations with physical activity (IPAQ), sleep quality (RCSQ), and health-related quality of life (Nottingham Health Profile). Honey consumption level was significantly associated with physical activity (6.8% of IPAQ variance), sleep quality (6.4% of RCSQ variance), and NHP scores (8.2% of variance), and among consumers IPAQ correlated positively with RCSQ (r=0.27) and negatively with NHP.

papers.title: Motor network neurophysiological (TMS-EEG) markers as predictors of outcomes of ventriculoperitoneal shunt sustained for over a year in normal pressure hydrocephalus.
papers.journal: Fluids and barriers of the CNS
papers.summary: In 41 patients with possible idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus, a TMS-EEG evoked-potential composite (Delphi-MD wave-form adherence, M1L WFA) was evaluated as a predictor of sustained (>1 year) response to ventriculoperitoneal shunt in 18 shunted patients. Baseline M1L WFA was higher in responders than non-responders (p=0.012) and discriminated them with ROC-AUC 0.935 and 90.9% sensitivity/85.7% specificity at a LOOCV-derived cutoff, whereas the CSF tap test did not predict shunt responsiveness.

papers.title: Effect of aerobic and Pilates exercise on balance, gait, functional capacity, lower extremity strength, fear of falling, sleep quality, and quality of life in older adults.
papers.summary: In this randomized controlled trial, 44 older adults aged 60-69 were assigned to 8 weeks of aerobic exercise (3 sessions/week) or Pilates (2 sessions/week) with equal total active exercise volume, and outcomes on balance, gait, function, strength, fear of falling, sleep, and quality of life were compared. Group × Time interactions favored aerobic exercise for gait velocity (10MWT, p=0.016) and dynamic balance (MBEST, p<0.001), while both interventions produced significant within-group improvements across remaining outcomes including 2MWT, 5xSTST, FES-I, PSQI, and WHOQOL-Brief domains.

papers.title: Parental Health Information Needs, Child-Health Literacy, and Use of Generative AI Among Parents of Children Aged 0 to 4 Years in France: A Cross-Sectional Study
papers.summary: This cross-sectional online survey of 12,634 French parents of children aged 0-47 months described child-health information needs, child-health literacy, and use of generative AI. Information needs were widespread and often unmet (61.8% searched without a clear reliable answer), literacy was generally high (median 3/4) but uneven with oral health weakest, and 54.2% had used AI for child-health questions, with 68.3% of trend-reporters increasing use over the year.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
